He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] from 2015 to 2018. McVeigh played for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian national team]] at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]]. McVeigh started his professional career with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the NBL in 2018 and spent three seasons with the team. He joined the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]] for their inaugural season in 2021 and led them to an [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] in 2024, earning the [[NBL Championship Series Most Valuable Player Award]]. During the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], he played for the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). ==Early life and career== McVeigh was born in [[Murwillumbah]], [[New South Wales]].{{cite web |title=Australia – 2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/8043/tid/239/_/2015_FIBA_U19_World_Championship/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=5 July 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160801074210/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/8043/tid/239/_/2015_FIBA_U19_World_Championship/index.html |archive-date=1 August 2016}}{{cite web |title=Jack McVeigh |url=https://www.olympics.com.au/olympians/jack-mcveigh/ |website=Australian Olympic Committee |access-date=16 July 2024}} He grew up in nearby [[Cabarita Beach, New South Wales|Cabarita Beach]] before moving to [[Gold Coast, Queensland|Gold Coast]] for [[boarding school]].{{cite web |title=Jack McVeigh - Why I've Decided to Start a Blog|url=https://www.jackmcveigh.com/post/why-am-i-starting-a-blog |website=jackmcveigh.com |accessdate=2 July 2022 |date=18 November 2021}} He attended [[The Southport School]]{{cite web |title=Buzzer-beater hero snaps back to reality |url=https://www.goldcoastbulletin.com.au/sport/local-sport/buzzerbeater-hero-snaps-back-to-reality/news-story/eca7906b6053d6b4c395dd49ed38a62c |website=Gold Coast Bulletin |accessdate=4 July 2022 |date=15 May 2018}} and played for the North Gold Coast Seahawks.{{cite web |title=Player Announcement - Jack McVeigh |url=https://www.seahawksbasketball.com.au/post/player-announcement-jack-mcveigh |website=North Gold Coast Seahawks |accessdate=6 July 2022 |date=20 January 2022}} He graduated from [[UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra|Lake Ginninderra College]] in [[Canberra]] in 2014.{{cite web|url=https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/season/2017-18/player/jack-mcveigh|title=Jack McVeigh|work=huskers.com|access-date=16 July 2024}} In 2014 and 2015, McVeigh played for the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Jack-McVeigh/328728|title=Jack McVeigh|work=australiabasket.com|access-date=28 March 2023|url-access=subscription}} ==College career== McVeigh played [[college basketball]] with the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] between 2015 and 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jack-mcveigh-1.html|title=Jack McVeigh|work=sports-reference.com|access-date=16 July 2024}} He emerged as the team's [[sixth man]] during his sophomore season but a reduction in playing time during his junior season led to his departure from the team.{{cite web |title=Former Husker basketball player Jack McVeigh signs with Australia's Adelaide 36ers |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/huskers/blogs/former-husker-basketball-player-jack-mcveigh-signs-with-australia-s/article_d0f112dd-36e1-5828-851c-963e7ae03cd1.html |website=Omaha World-Herald |accessdate=15 November 2019 |date=23 April 2018}} In 78 games over three seasons, he made 15 starts and averaged 5.3 points and 2.3 rebounds in 17.6 minutes per game. ==Professional career== ===NBL, state leagues and Germany (2018–2024)=== After leaving college, McVeigh returned to his hometown to play for the [[Gold Coast Rollers (NBL1 North)|Gold Coast Rollers]] in the 2018 [[Queensland Basketball League]] season. He subsequently joined the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] on a three-year deal.{{cite web |title=36ers sign McVeigh on a three-year deal |url=http://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/article/36ers-sign-mcveigh-on-a-three-year-deal |website=Adelaide 36ers |accessdate=15 November 2019}} He averaged 3.4 points and 1.8 rebounds with the 36ers in [[2018–19 NBL season|2018–19]]. He then played for the [[North Adelaide Rockets]] in the 2019 [[NBL1 Central|Premier League]] season. He averaged 6.0 points in [[2019–20 NBL season|2019–20]]{{cite web |title=Jack McVeigh |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/players/jack-mcveigh |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=30 January 2026}} and 9.4 points in [[2020–21 NBL season|2020–21]].{{cite news |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=NBL Free Agency: who's on the move |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/31715766/nbl-free-agency-move |access-date=29 June 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=26 June 2021}} He re-joined the North Adelaide Rockets, now in the [[NBL1 Central]], for the [[2021 NBL1 season]], helping them win the [[List of NBL1 Central champions|NBL1 Central championship]].{{cite web |title=Rockets set to launch with signings of star 36ers duo |url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/rockets-set-to-launch-with-signings-of-star-36ers-duo/ |website=NBL1.com.au |access-date=11 April 2021 |date=9 April 2021}}{{cite web |title=Rocket-Men fly to first since 2007 |url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/rocket-men-fly-to-first-since-2007/central/ |website=NBL1.com.au |access-date=28 March 2023 |date=11 September 2021}} McVeigh joined the inaugural squad of the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]], a team entering the NBL for the first time in [[2021–22 NBL season|2021–22]].{{Cite web|title=Jack McVeigh Signs with the JackJumpers|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/jack-mcveigh-signs-with-the-jackjumpers|website=NBL.com.au|date=6 July 2021|access-date=6 July 2021}} He helped the JackJumpers reach the 2022 NBL Grand Final series, where they lost 3–0 to the [[Sydney Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/kings-win-first-championship-in-17-years-with-record-crowd|title=Kings Win First Championship in 17 Years with Record Crowd|work=NBL.com.au|date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 May 2022}} After playing for the North Gold Coast Seahawks of the [[NBL1 North]] in the [[2022 NBL1 season]],{{cite web |title=Championship Rocket joins brother in NBL1 North |url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/championship-rocket-joins-brother-in-nbl1-north |website=NBL1 |access-date=19 April 2022 |date=21 January 2022}} McVeigh re-joined the JackJumpers for the [[2022–23 NBL season]]. Following the NBL season, he joined [[USC Heidelberg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] for the end of the [[2022–23 Basketball Bundesliga|2022–23 BBL season]].{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Heidelberg tabs Jack McVeigh, ex Tasmania JJ |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Germany/news/795862/Heidelberg-tabs-Jack-McVeigh,-ex-Tasmania-JJ |website=Eurobasket |access-date=27 February 2023 |date=27 February 2023}} In the [[2023–24 NBL season]], the JackJumpers reached the NBL Championship Series with a 2–1 victory over the [[Perth Wildcats]] in the semi-finals, with McVeigh scoring a game-high and career-high 27 points in game three.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/jackjumpers-dominant-in-playoff-decider|title=JackJumpers dominant in Playoff 2024}} The JackJumpers went on to win the [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] with a 3–2 Championship Series victory over [[Melbourne United]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/tasmania-jackjumpers-nbl24-champions|title=Tasmania JackJumpers: NBL24 Champions|work=NBL.com.au|date=31 March Championship Series Most Valuable Player Award|Championship Series MVP]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/mcveigh-named-nbl24-sengstock-trophy-winner|title=McVeigh named NBL24 Sengstock Trophy winner|work=NBL.com.au|date=31 March 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240331082236/https://nbl.com.au/news/mcveigh-named-nbl24-sengstock-trophy-winner|archive-date=31 web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/jackjumpers-set-to-re-sign-stars|title=JackJumpers set to re-sign stars|work=NBL.com.au|date=6 April 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240406035201/https://nbl.com.au/news/jackjumpers-set-to-re-sign-stars|archive-date=6 April 2024}} On 12 April 2024, McVeigh extended his (2024–2025)=== On 25 July 2024, McVeigh signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Jack McVeigh to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-jack-mcveigh-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=25 July 2024|access-date=25 July 2024}} He became the first NBA player to wear the jersey number 58 which is the sum of the four jersey numbers he wore during his collegiate, NBL and international careers.{{cite web |last1=Feigen |first1=Jonathan |title=What's in a number? For Houston Rockets' Jack McVeigh, a piece of NBA history |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/rockets/article/jack-mcveigh-nba-number-58-19821183.php |website=Houston Chronicle |access-date=8 November 2024 |date=7 October 2024}} McVeigh made his debut for the Rockets in a game against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on 6 November and scored his first points with a three-pointer against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] two days later.{{cite web |title=Dyson Daniels, Josh Giddey, Jack McVeigh and Luke Travers are key talking points for Australians in the NBA |url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/nba/dyson-daniels-josh-giddey-jack-mcveigh-and-luke-travers-are-key-talking-points-for-australians-in-the-nba-c-16704491 |website=The West Australian |access-date=11 November 2024 |date=11 November 2024}} On 9 January 2025, he scored a career-high 29 points in the Vipers' 130–118 win over the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite news |title=Career-High for McVeigh Puts Vipers Past Blue |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/career-high-for-mcveigh-puts-vipers-past-blue/n-6179955 |access-date=12 January 2025 |work=OurSports Central |date=9 January 2025 |language=en}} McVeigh played in nine NBA games but spent most of the [[2024–25 Houston Rockets season|2024–25 season]] with the Vipers where he averaged 15.7 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game across 37 G League appearances.{{cite news |title=No NBA deal, no panic: McVeigh eyes Next Shot |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/no-nba-deal-no-panic-mcveigh-eyes-next-shot |access-date=30 June 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=30 June 2025}} McVeigh joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news |last1=Bredeson |first1=Evan |date=6 July 2025 |title=Former Nebraska basketball player signs with the Atlanta Hawks for the NBA summer league |url=https://cornhuskerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/cornhuskers/mens-basketball/2025/07/06/nebraska-basketball-jack-mcveigh-atlanta-hawks-houston-rockets-las-vegas/84481883007/ |access-date=6 July 2025 |work=Cornhuskers Wire|publisher=USA Today}} On 3 August 2025, the JackJumpers released McVeigh from the remainder of his contract.{{cite web |title=Club Statement: Jack McVeigh |url=https://www.jackjumpers.com.au/news/club-statement-jack-mcveigh |website=Tasmania JackJumpers |access-date=4 August 2025 |date=3 August 2025}} ===Cairns Taipans (2025–present)=== On 5 August 2025, McVeigh signed with the [[Cairns Taipans]] of the NBL on a two-year deal, with the second year being a mutual option.{{Cite web |title=McVeigh returns to the NBL, chooses Cairns |url=https://www.taipans.com/news/mcveigh-returns-to-the-nbl-chooses-cairns |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=Cairns Taipans {{!}} Official NBL Website |date=5 August 2025}} On 16 October, he was sidelined with a wrist injury.{{cite news |title=Injury sidelines Taipans' marquee man |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/injury-sidelines-key-taipan-jack-mcveigh |access-date=16 October 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=16 October 2025 |language=en}} On 16 November, McVeigh scored a career-high 39 points in a 105–101 overtime loss to the [[Adelaide 36ers]].{{cite news |title=OT Sixers win after Cotton/McVeigh show |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/ot-sixers-win-after-cotton-mcveigh-show |access-date=16 November 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=16 November 2025 |language=en}} Six days later, he had his second straight 30-point game, finishing with 35 points in a 102–96 loss to the [[New Zealand Breakers]].{{cite news |title=Breakers stand firm to complete Cairns win |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/breakers-stand-firm-to-complete-cairns-win |access-date=22 November 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=22 November 2025 |language=en}} On 19 December, he set a new career high with 47 points in a 99–95 win over the Breakers.{{cite news |title=McVeigh unstoppable as Snakes beat Breakers |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/mcveigh-unstoppable-as-snakes-beat-breakers |access-date=19 December 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=19 December 2025 |language=en}} On 22 January 2026, he scored 34 points with eight 3-pointers in a 106–69 loss to the [[Perth Wildcats]].{{cite news |title=Pepper inspires hot Wildcats shooting night |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/pepper-inspires-hot-wildcats-shooting-night |access-date=22 January 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=22 January 2026 |language=en}} On 30 January, he scored 40 points in a 96–93 overtime win over the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]], playing all 45 minutes.{{cite news |title=McVeigh's 40 lifts Snakes over JackJumpers |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/mcveighs-40-lifts-snakes-over-jackjumpers |access-date=30 January 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=30 January 2026 |language=en}} He was named to the [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL |work=nbl.com.au |date=23 February 2026 |language=en}} On 12 February 2026, McVeigh and the Taipans agreed to the mutual option on his contract for the [[2026–27 NBL season]].{{cite news |title=Jack
